touches.text: The abstract ticket owns what every kind shares: its birth (cast) and its three parts, each with one job: the plan (only what a builder builds from), the metadata and state (what gates and doors read and write as it moves), and the history (the append-only log). WHY: one job per part reduces confusion; a builder reads the plan and nothing else (Akien, 2026-10-29 and 2026-11-02).
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
Has its own workflow stamped on it (the state string, with the cursor).
Each workflow step declares what it needs.
Lives in CairnCommons/tickets/ while staged; its trail migrates beside its code as that component's history while under way, and back to the commons after (Law 5).
The ticket owns its refusals: a gate refuses a crossing on the ticket's behalf (ruling 2026-08-10). The gates are CodeMother's (10.3.5).
gate: the == compare, in one place. A gate opens when every expected equals its actual. No oracle, ever.

ROOT INTENTION for checks and gates (Akien, 2026-10-27): the inspector does all the checks, so there is no need for more checks anywhere else. The inspector's output is consumed by the gate. The gate's output is the certificate. "This was how I meant it all along."

The inspectors are not assumed correct; they are examined when they refuse. A failure is not automatically "it broke, change it". After a gate refuses, an LLM sets the refusing sieve's intention and why beside the ticket's intention and why and asks: is this sieve the best we can do right now? If yes, the ticket changes. If no, the sieve is fixed. Either way the system improves, constantly. WHY: questions about a part are answered by its intention and why against the new thing's intention and why, so a disagreement becomes an update to an intention or to its implementation plan, never a conversation about procedure (Akien, 2026-11-02). The sieves stay deterministic and never weigh a why; the LLM check comes only after a failure. It is never a lock pick because it has no third outcome: the ticket changes, or the sieve is fixed through its own ticket and proof. Nothing passes a ticket over a red; testing a sieve is what the ticket that fixes it does. (Q#62, Akien 2026-11-02.)

x, new or changed code (code-seam): at BUILDME the named proof exists and its PROVES names the ticket, and it may be red, since a new proof is red before its build. At PROVED it is sealed green and hollow-measured.

y, fixit (bug): at BUILDME the ticket names the red it fixes (the proof), and that proof really is red on disk now; the named proof may be red, fixing it is the job. The fix may change the test case itself without a ruling: the proof's why names the ticket and says what it tests and why it changed, and names any tooth it removed. At PROVED it is sealed green and hollow-measured, as x.

skills/ (cairnhelp, challenge, chart, commit, intent, sorted, ...): Claude Code skills. The deterministic parts move out of markdown into CC device verbs: a skill's OS-side work runs as a script, and CC's shim processes the result and injects it into the session. Why: every habit captured that way is one CC no longer spends inference on, so CC gets faster. Precedent: UU's first charting pass did the first 3 or 4 steps in deterministic Python with no LLM until after, which saved about 90% of tokens, measured in real use. (Q#56, Akien 2026-11-05)
